tei:div.tei:ab: I. 1927 (schriftlich): Urlinie zu Scarlatti Cdur 32; Volksausgabe; korrigiert im Januar 27.Diary January 3, 1927: “From Cube (letter): Urlinie of Scarlatti's C major [Sonata], No. 32 of the Volksausgabe[Leipzig: Breitkopf & Härtel, c. 1882]”; January 14: “10:30 with Brahms–Scarlatti, completed for the second time, finally to Cube's Urlinie.”; January 16: – “To Cube (letter): correction of his Urlinie.”; January 26: “From Cube (letter): he thanks me for the corrections, is already teaching at the Conservatory in Duisburg.”; – January 31: “To Cube (postcard): greetings; do not omit the linear progressions, however the solution may turn out.”
January 1927 (in writing): Urlinie for Scarlatti’s Sonata in C major, No. 32 of the Volksausgabe; corrected in January 1927.

tei:div.tei:ab: October 17 On the Urlinie in Beethoven’s Op. 10, No. 1; Chopin Etude Op. 25, No. 2 in F minor, bars 1–4.
November 3 Continuation of the fingering of the Etude.
November 5 Back to two-voice counterpoint, first species; many assignments corrected.
November 7 Urlinie graph of the Etude completed.
October November 14 Urlinie and playing united.

October November 17 Mozart Sonata in A major, new; Urlinie of the theme, playing
of 1–4.
November 19 Three-voice counterpoint, reply to numerous questions.
November 21 On solmization; Mozart theme continued.
December 17 Assignments in two- and three-voice counterpoint corrected.
December 24 On the second species of three-voice counterpoint.
January 14 Something about Mozart's Symphony in G minor and about Beethoven’s Symphony in C minor.
January 16 Chopin Etude in F major from Op. 10 No. ?, new.
January 23 The Urlinie of this Etude continued, then the work played.
January 26 Mozart Minuet; he attempts an Urlinie, and fingering.
January 28 Third species of three-voice counterpoint; assignments in two- and three-voice counterpoint.
February 6 Schubert Waltzes op. 9, Urlinie of the first waltz corrected.
February 11 Schubert Waltzes No. 2; he corrects the Urlinie.
February 13 Etude in F major completed and played.
February 18 Schubert Waltzes Nos 3 and 4 corrected (instead of counterpoint exercises).
February 20 Exercises relating to the F major Etude, prepared by himself, corrected; on Beethoven’s Seventh Symphony (in relation to Breisach)’s concert.
February 25 Tied notes in two-voice counterpoint.
March 4 Tied notes in three-voice counterpoint.
March 16 He brings the first edition of the partita by J. S. Bach, and organ fantasies; shows the attempt at an Urlinie for the Sarabande.
March 18 Tied notes in three-voice counterpoint; he shows me a Couperin first edition.
March 20 On the Cello Sonata in A major (Casals); on Stravinksy’s Piano Concerto.
March 23 Critique of Casals’s performance; Hoboken shows me the notes that he made in his lesson booklet while Casals was playing – a nice accomplishment.

March 25 Fifth
species of two-voice counterpoint.
March 27 Graph of the Trio from the Minuet.
March 30 On the St. Matthew Passion (Klenau); the Rondo alla turca begun.
April 1 Continuation of the fifth species and tied notes in three-voice counterpoint.
April 6 He brings Vrieslander with him.
April 8 Tied notes in three-voice counterpoint.
April 13 At Rothberger’s place, for afternoon snack.
April 17 Attempt at Haydn’s Sonata in G minor: sketch and fingering begun.
April 20 Haydn set aside, in the absence of a suitable edition; in its place, Beethoven’s Op. 14, No. 2.
April 29 Assignment in mixed-species counterpoint; Bruckner’s Seventh Symphony taken home, for preparation.
May 5 First movement of Bruckner’s Seventh Symphony played.
May 6 Mixed-species counterpoint continued; remarks on “Leonora” Overture No. 3.

May 11 Beethoven sonata as far as
the recapitulation.
May 25 Some things about Mozart’s Don Giovanni; aids to synthesis in Mendelssohn’s “Scottish” Symphony.
May 27 Mozart’s Symphony, first movement, shown; mistakes in the score; I urge him to have a facsimile made.

May 29 He brings the newly acquired parts for the G minor Symphony, in the oldest print by André, a rare example of the most faithful reproduction of the autograph manuscript; he also shows me the first edition of Mozart’s Adagio in B minor K. 540 and his independently identified Andante by Haydn, which I, however, declare to be inauthentic; I show him voice-leading in Handel’s Lessons in B major and in the variations; voice-leading progressions also in Bach’s Fugue in E minor.
June 1 I show him mistakes in the scores of Mozart’s symphony.
June 5 He declares himself prepared to have a facsimile edition made of the Symphony in E major too!

tei:div.tei:ab: 7. XI. Beethoven op. 10 No 2; Chopin, Berçeuse, kleiner Walzer Gesd.
21. XI. op. 111 (besser); Chopin Nocturne Fisdur u. Berçeuse.
2. I. Fortsetzung der Etuden op. 25 u. Walzer Asdur op. ?.
16. I. Mozart Sonate Adur; Chopin Walzer Cismoll.

19. II. Appassionata (sehr gut); Chopin Mazurka Hmoll,Probably the Mazurka in B minor Op. 33, No. 4; Op. 30, No. 2, begins in B minor but gravitates towards F minor and ends in that key. (Schenker would have questioned the tonality of Op. 30, No. 2, as he did the second Scherzo, Op. 31.) It is more difficult to identify the other mazurkas mentioned here. neu; wiederholt Gmoll, Cdur.

7. V. Brahms-Paganini-Variationen 1. u. 2. HeftIn a recommendation of Miss Kahn to Otto Erich Deutsch (I.N. 191-566, August 5, 1930), Schenker remarks: “She plays from memory at one sitting Brahms's Paganini Variations, Chopin's complete Etudes Op. 10 and Op. 25, Beethoven's Op. 106, etc.” – trotz Fehlern eine schöne Leistung; Chopin Walzer Asdur, Cismoll, Fdur wiederholt.

21. V. Chopin Ballade
wiederholt; Bach Gavotte Dm aus einer englischen Suite.

5. VI. Etuden von Chopin, sehr gut,In a recommendation of Miss Kahn to Otto Erich Deutsch (I.N. 191-566, August 5, 1930), Schenker remarks: “She plays from memory at one sitting Brahms's Paganini Variations, Chopin's complete Etudes Op. 10 and Op. 25, Beethoven's Op. 106, etc.” ausgenommen op. 25, No 2.

tei:div.tei:ab: October 3: Op. 109; Chopin Prelude in G major.
October 17: Brahms Handel Variations; I correct only as far as the Fugue.
November 7: Beethoven Op. 10, No. 2; Chopin, Berceuse, short waltz in G major
November 21: Op. 111 (better); Chopin Nocturne in F major and Berceuse.
December 7: Op. 110; Nocturne in F major.
December 19: Chopin Etudes from Op. 10 and Op. 25.
January 2: Continuation of the Etudes Op. 25, and one of the waltzes in A major.
January 16: Mozart Sonata in A major; Chopin Waltz in C minor.
February 19: “Appassionata” Sonata (very good); Chopin Mazurka in B minor, new; those in G minor and C major revisited.
April 17: Several nocturnes, and the Berceuse.
May 7: Brahms “Paganini” Variations, books 1 and 2 – a beautiful achievement in spite of mistakes; Chopin waltzes in A major, C minor and F major revisited.

May 21: Chopin Ballade
repeated; Bach, Gavotte in D minor from an English Suite.
June 5: Etudes by Chopin, very good, except for Op. 25, No. 2.

tei:div.tei:ab: 5. X. Brahms-Händel-Variationen bis zur Fuge wiederholt.
12. X. Fragen zu einzelnen Variationen; Chopin Etude op. 25 No 2 neu.
9. XI. Wiederholt den letzten Satz der Mondschein-Sonate.
16. XI. Mozart bis zur Adagio Variation.
30. XI. Letzte Variation; 1. u. 2. Satz der Mondschein-Sonate.
28. XII. Die ganze Sonate wiederholt; Chopin Scherzo Bmoll begonnen.

8. II. Scherzo wieder-
-holt; Schumann „Eintritt in den Wald“.
1. III. Wiederholungen, auch Schumann „Vogel als Prophet“; op. 57 fortgesetzt.
15. III. op. 57 bis zur Coda; Schumann wiederholt.
13. V. Abgeschlossen.Diary May 13, 1926: “I give [substitute] lessons in lieu of June 28 to Dr. Brünauer, Miss Mosčisker, and Mrs. Pairamall.”
6. VI. Bis Ende der Saison Wiederholungen.

tei:div.tei:ab: October 5: Brahms Handel Variations as far as the fugue, revisited.
October 12: Questions about individual variations; Chopin Etude, Op. 25, No. 2, new.
October 26: Mozart Sonata in A major, new.
November 9: The last movement of the “Moonlight” Sonata revisited.
November 16: Mozart as far as the Adagio variation.
November 23: The Adagio variation; “Moonlight” Sonata, first movement.
November 30: Last variation; first and second movements of the “Moonlight” Sonata.
December 28: The entire sonata revisited; Chopin Scherzo B minor begun.
February 1: Schumann Forest Scenes revisited: “Lonely Flowers”.

February 8: Scherzo revisited
; Schumann “Entry into the Wood”.
March 1: Revisitings, also Schumann “Bird as Prophet”; Op. 57 continued.
March 15: Op. 57 as far as the coda; Schumann revisited.
April 12: Andante and first two variations.
June 6: Revisitations until the end of the teaching year.

tei:div.tei:ab: 23. X. (1. Stunde!) Chopin Mazurka op. 56 No 1 (Hdur); op. 50 No 3 (Cismoll), neu.Diary Oct 30, 1925: “In the evening, I work on the two mazurkas for Mrs. Pairamall.”

16. XI. Mazurka Fismoll op. 59 No 3 ganz falsch aufgefaßt, ebenso op. 33 No 2 (Ddur).Diary Nov 16: “Mrs. Pairamall brings Chopin mazurkas in the edition of Gebethner as a present, also Zweig’s Three Daemons to read.”
23. XI. Nocturne Fisdur op. 15 No 2, neu.
30. XI. Mazurka Amoll wiederholt.Chopin wrote four mazurkas in the key of A minor but made extensive analytical notes on only one of these, Op. 17, No.4.

14. XII. Mazurka Hmoll op. 30 No 2 neu; Mazurka Cisdur op. 50 No 2,The C- minor mazurka from Chopin’s Op. 50 is No. 3, not No. 2. But Schenker marks the work as “new,” and he had already marked Op. 50, No. 3, as a new work at Pairamall’s lesson on October 23, 1925. So he may be referring to a different C minor mazurka, or to the Mazurka in A major, Op. 50, No. 2. neu.
28. XII. Nocturne Hdur, Mittelteil, Fingersatz; wiederholt Walzer Cismoll, Mittelteil.
4. I. Nocturne Hdur wiederholt, Etude Gism aus op. 25.
11. I. Etude Cmoll aus op. 10 No 12 wiederholt.
18. I. Wiederholt Etude F dur moll op. 10 No 9; Cdur No 7.
25. I. Etude Fmoll op. 10 u. Urlinie-Fragen im Allgemeinen.
8. II. Schubert Impromptu Esdur wiederholt; Chopin Nocturne Cismoll wiederholt u. Fingersatz.Diary Feb 7, 1926: “I work on Chopin's Nocturne in C minor (for Mrs. Pairamall).”
1. III. Schubert Impromptu Asdur, Trio Cismoll statt Desmoll, Vortrag, namentlich Begleitung.

8. III. Bringt Stücke von Rozizky;Ludomir Różycki (1883–1953), Polish composer, who wrote numerous works for solo piano in traditional 19th-century genres (ballades, fantasy pieces, impromptus, intermezzos, nocturnes, and preludes). – Mrs. Pairamall was herself Polish and Schenker was quite liberal in allowing her to play Polish pieces she brought in. Chopin Mazurka Cismoll mit phrygischem d, neu.Chopin wrote five mazurkas in the key of C minor; from Schenker’s reference to “Phrygian d,” the lowered second step of the C minor scale, one can identify this work as Op. 41, No. 1.

15. III. Ueber Ganche, Frl. Dubois usw.;Édouard Ganche (1880–1945) wrote several books about Chopin, including Frédéric Chopin: sa vie et ses œuvres 1810–1849 (Paris: Mercure de France, 1913). Camille Dubois (née O’Meara, 1825–1907) was born in Paris of Irish parents; she studied with Chopin before becoming a concert pianist. The “Miss Dubois” to whom Schenker refers may have been her daughter or granddaughter. bringt „Belege“; über Casals;Schenker’s diary for March 22, in an extended description, gives: “Casals’s concert (with Schulhof): Beethoven’s Sonata Op. 69 is not performed! […] a Prelude by [Emmanuel] Moór […] [Bach’s] unaccompanied Suite in C minor […] two pieces by Schumann, “Langsam” and “Mit Humor” […], a sonata by Bréval.” Chro-
-matische Fantasie wiederholt bis zum Rezitativ.
19. IV. Chopin-Handschrift zurückerstattet; Chromatische Fuge wiederholt.Diary April 19, 1926: “Mrs Pairamall appears again and pays; I return the Chopin autograph manuscript to her.”
26. IV. Nocturne Hdur op. 9 u. Fisdur op. 15 wiederholt.
13. V. Nocturne Fdur, neu.Diary May 13, 1926: “I give [substitute] lessons in lieu of June 28 to Dr. Brünauer, Miss Mosčisker, and Mrs. Pairamall.”
17. V. Noch einmal Nocturn Cismoll, Mittelpartie.

31. V. Schenkt Litzmanns „Clara Schumann“Berthold Litzmann, Clara Schumann: ein Künstlerleben, 3 vols. (Leipzig, 1902–08). Schenker’s diary for this date records: “Mrs. Pairamall gives us Litzmann's Clara Schumann.”

tei:div.tei:ab: October 23: (first lesson!). Chopin Mazurka Op. 56, No. 1 (B major); Op. 50, No. 3 (C minor), new.
November 16: Mazurka in F minor, Op. 59, No. 3, completely misinterpreted, likewise Op. 33, No. 2 (D major).
November 23: Nocturne in Fp major, Op. 15, No. 2, new.
November 30: Mazurka in A minor revisited.
December 7: Chopin Waltz in C minor revisited.
December 14: Mazurka in B minor, Op. 30, No. 2, new; Mazurka in C minor, Op. 50, No. 2, new.
December 21: Nocturne in B major from Op. 9 revisited.
December 28: Nocturne in B major, middle section, fingering; the middle section of the Waltz in C minor revisited.
January 4: Nocturne in B major revisited; Etude in G minor from Op. 25.
January 11: Etude in C minor, Op. 10, No. 12, revisited.
January 18: Etude in F minor, Op. 10, No. 9 revisited; C major, No. 7.
January 25: Etude in F minor from Op. 10 and questions about the Urlinie in general.
February 1: Nocturne in C minor, new.
February 8: Schubert Impromptu in E major revisited; Chopin Nocturne C minor revisited, and fingering.
February 15: Schubert Impromptu in A major.
March 1: Schubert Impromptu in A major, Trio section written in C minor instead of D minor: performance, especially of the accompaniment.
March 8: She brings pieces by Rozizky; Chopin Mazurka in C minor with the Phrygian d, new.

March 15: Concerning Ganche, Miss Dubois, etc.; she brings “evidence”; about Casals;
Chromatic Fantasy revisited as far as the recitative.
April 19: Chopin manuscript returned; Chromatic Fugue revisited.
April 26: Nocturnes in B major from Op. 9 and F major from Op. 15 revisited.
May 10: Nocturne in C minor revisited.
May 13: Nocturne in F major, new.
May 17: Once more the Nocturne in C minor, middle section.
May 31: She makes a present of Litzmann’s Clara Schumann.

20. I.: In op. 111: Der Schlusstriller u. mein Fingersatz; Antwort: 15/35/35 u. 45/45, nicht trillermäßig 153/535, nicht 454/5; dann Brahms Streichquartett Cm, 2. Satz, Tonart Fm oder Cm? Antwort: Fm.Diary January 23: “To Weisse (postcard): I explain the misunderstanding regarding the fingering and the tonality question arising from I–III–V, for which the recapitulation offers the proof at the analogous point – thus Brahms is in the right, in spite of his (Weisse's) opinion.” — The postcard in question is not known to survive. — Schenker draws a five-line stave below to mark the end of the saison’s notes.

January 20: In Op. 111: the concluding trill, and my fingering; answer: 15/35/35 and 45/45, not in the manner of a trill 153/535, not 454/545. Then: Brahms’s String Quartet in C minor, second movement, is it in the key of F minor or C minor? Answer: F minor.
